latest_final: The puzzle turns on ambiguity between academic courses and the "courses" of a meal. The student is at a university and must "choose courses before the deadline," but the relevant "courses" are the successive dishes of a formal dinner he attended, chosen in advance. During that single evening, the dinner proceeded dish by dish: each chosen course was brought out, served, and then cleared away as the next arrived, so the meal was consumed course by course within that one evening. Thus "all of my courses were gone in one evening" does not mean a registration system lost his enrollments; it means the multi-course dinner was served and taken away over that one evening, and by the end every course had literally gone. The "deadline" was the dinner's advance selection date, and the pun on "courses" is the solution.
